tasks.title: Project and Environment Setup
tasks.description: Initialize the project repository, create a standard directory structure, and set up the Python virtual environment for the project.
tasks.details: Create a `requirements.txt` file listing all necessary dependencies, including PyTorch, torchvision, and Pillow. Initialize a Git repository for version control.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the virtual environment can be created and dependencies can be installed successfully using `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

subtasks.title: Develop API Endpoints for User Profile Management
subtasks.description: Create and implement the backend API endpoints required for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting user profiles.
subtasks.details: Implement RESTful endpoints: POST /api/users, GET /api/users/{id}, PUT /api/users/{id}, DELETE /api/users/{id}. Use a database model for the user profile including fields like 'username', 'email', 'fullName', and 'creationDate'. Ensure proper input validation and error handling for all endpoints. Secure the endpoints using token-based authentication.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for the controller and service layers to verify business logic. Use integration tests to validate the full request/response cycle for each endpoint, including database interactions. Test edge cases like invalid input, non-existent user IDs, and unauthorized access attempts.

subtasks.title: Build Frontend User Profile Page
subtasks.description: Develop the user interface for displaying and editing a user's profile information, consuming the API endpoints from the first subtask.
subtasks.details: Create a new route and component for '/profile/{id}'. The page should fetch user data from the GET /api/users/{id} endpoint upon loading. Display the user information in a clear, readable format. Include an 'Edit' button that enables a form to update the user's data. The form submission should call the PUT /api/users/{id} endpoint. Handle API responses to show success or error notifications to the user.
subtasks.testStrategy: Perform manual UI testing to ensure the layout is responsive and all interactive elements work as expected. Write end-to-end tests using a framework like Cypress or Playwright to simulate a user viewing their profile, entering edit mode, changing data, and saving the changes. Mock the API endpoints to test the frontend component in isolation.

tasks.title: Develop Data Loading and Preprocessing Module
tasks.description: Create a Python module to handle loading and preprocessing of the training images. This module will prepare the data for consumption by the PyTorch model.
tasks.details: The module must be able to load 1920x1080 RGB JPG images, apply necessary transformations (e.g., resizing, tensor conversion, normalization), and create PyTorch `Dataset` and `DataLoader` objects. It should also handle splitting the 300 sample images into training and validation sets.
tasks.testStrategy: Confirm that the DataLoader produces batches of correctly shaped and normalized tensors without errors.

subtasks.title: Create PyTorch Dataset class
subtasks.description: Implement a class that inherits from `torch.utils.data.Dataset` to load image file paths and labels from the `fireballs`, `meteors`, and `no_meteors` directories.
subtasks.details: The custom Dataset class should scan the subdirectories to build a list of image paths and their corresponding integer labels. The `__getitem__` method should load an image by its index, apply transformations, and return the image tensor and its label.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the Dataset object can be instantiated and that `__getitem__` returns a tensor and a correct integer label for a given index.

subtasks.title: Define Image Transformations
subtasks.description: Create a composition of `torchvision.transforms` to resize images to a consistent input size (e.g., 224x224), convert them to PyTorch tensors, and normalize them using standard ImageNet statistics.
subtasks.details: Use `torchvision.transforms.Compose` to chain together `Resize`, `ToTensor`, and `Normalize`. This transform pipeline will be passed to the custom Dataset class during its initialization.
subtasks.testStrategy: Apply the transform pipeline to a sample image and check the output tensor's shape (e.g., `[3, 224, 224]`), data type, and value range to confirm it's ready for the model.

subtasks.title: Implement Data Splitting and DataLoaders
subtasks.description: Add logic to split the dataset into training and validation sets (e.g., 80/20 split). Create `torch.utils.data.DataLoader` instances for both sets to handle batching and shuffling.
subtasks.details: Use `torch.utils.data.random_split` to divide the main dataset into training and validation subsets. Then, instantiate two `DataLoader` objects, one for each subset. The training DataLoader should have `shuffle=True`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Iterate through one batch of the training and validation DataLoaders. Confirm that each produces a batch of image tensors and a batch of label tensors with the correct dimensions.

tasks.title: Define CNN Model Architecture
tasks.description: Design and implement the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture using the PyTorch framework.
tasks.details: The model will be a Python class inheriting from `torch.nn.Module`. It must be designed to take preprocessed image tensors as input and output predictions for the three categories: 'fireballs', 'regular meteors', and 'no meteors'.
tasks.testStrategy: Instantiate the model and pass a dummy tensor of the correct input shape through it to ensure the forward pass executes and produces an output tensor of the correct shape (batch_size, 3).

subtasks.title: Create Model File
subtasks.description: Create a new Python file at `src/model.py` to house the neural network architecture.

subtasks.title: Implement CNN Architecture
subtasks.description: Define a class `NightSkyCNN` that inherits from `torch.nn.Module`. This class will contain the layers of the convolutional neural network (e.g., convolutional layers, ReLU activation, max pooling, and fully-connected layers).

subtasks.title: Define Forward Pass
subtasks.description: Implement the `forward` method within the `NightSkyCNN` class to define the flow of data through the network layers.

tasks.title: Implement Model Training Script
tasks.description: Create a script to train the CNN model on the prepared dataset and save the resulting weights.
tasks.details: The script will contain the training loop, define a loss function (e.g., CrossEntropyLoss) and an optimizer (e.g., Adam), and perform training for a set number of epochs. After training, it must save the trained model's state dictionary to a file (e.g., `model.pth`).
tasks.testStrategy: Run the script and verify that training loss decreases over several epochs and that a model weight file is created upon completion.

subtasks.title: Create Training Script File
subtasks.description: Create a new Python file at `src/train.py`.

subtasks.title: Implement Training Loop
subtasks.description: In `src/train.py`, write the main training loop that iterates through the training data for a specified number of epochs.

subtasks.title: Define Loss Function and Optimizer
subtasks.description: Instantiate the loss function (e.g., `nn.CrossEntropyLoss`) and the optimizer (e.g., `torch.optim.Adam`).

subtasks.title: Save Trained Model
subtasks.description: After the training loop is complete, save the trained model's state dictionary to a file named `night_sky_model.pth`.

tasks.title: Develop Command-Line Interface (CLI) Script
tasks.description: Create the main Python script that serves as the command-line tool for image classification.
tasks.details: Use Python's `argparse` module to implement a CLI that accepts exactly one argument: the absolute path to a directory of images. The script should include basic structure for file processing.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute the script from the command line with a test path and verify that it correctly parses the argument and doesn't raise an error. Test with no arguments or too many arguments to ensure it fails gracefully.

subtasks.title: Create CLI script file
subtasks.description: Create a new Python file at `src/main.py`.

subtasks.title: Implement argument parsing
subtasks.description: Use Python's `argparse` module to define and parse the command-line arguments.

tasks.title: Implement Directory Creation Logic
tasks.description: Add functionality to the CLI script to create the required output subdirectories.
tasks.details: Within the target directory provided via the command line, the script must create three subdirectories: `fireballs`, `meteors`, and `no_meteors`. This creation should only happen if they do not already exist.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the script on a new empty directory and verify the three subdirectories are created. Run it again on the same directory to ensure no errors occur.

subtasks.title: Implement directory creation logic
subtasks.description: Use `os.makedirs` with `exist_ok=True` to create the output directories.

tasks.title: Implement Image File Iteration Logic
tasks.description: Add logic to the CLI script to find and iterate through the target image files.
tasks.details: The script must iterate through every file with a `.jpg` extension located in the root of the specified directory. It must ignore files in subdirectories (including the newly created category folders) and files with other extensions.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a test directory containing `.jpg` files, `.txt` files, and subdirectories with more `.jpg` files. Run the script and log the files it intends to process, verifying it only selects the root-level `.jpg` files.

subtasks.title: Implement image file iteration logic
subtasks.description: Use `os.listdir` and `fname.lower().endswith(".jpg")` to iterate through the image files.

tasks.title: Integrate Model for Inference
tasks.description: Load the pre-trained PyTorch model into the CLI script and use it to predict the category for each image.
tasks.details: The script will load the saved `model.pth` file. For each image being processed, it will apply the same preprocessing transformations used during training, perform a forward pass through the model, and determine the predicted class label.
tasks.testStrategy: Pass a single test image through the inference function and verify that it returns one of the three expected category strings: 'fireballs', 'meteors', or 'no_meteors'.

subtasks.title: Load pre-trained model
subtasks.description: Load the saved `night_sky_model.pth` file into the model.

subtasks.title: Preprocess images for inference
subtasks.description: Apply the same transformations used during training to the images that will be classified.

subtasks.title: Perform model inference
subtasks.description: Perform a forward pass through the model to get the prediction.

tasks.title: Implement File Moving Functionality
tasks.description: Move each processed image file into its corresponding category subfolder based on the model's prediction.
tasks.details: After an image is classified by the model, use a library like `shutil` to move the image file from the source directory to the appropriate subfolder (`fireballs`, `meteors`, or `no_meteors`).
tasks.testStrategy: Run the full script on a test directory with several images. Verify that all original `.jpg` files are gone from the root directory and are now located inside the correct category subdirectories.

subtasks.title: Implement file moving logic
subtasks.description: Use `os.rename` to move the classified files to the correct subdirectories.

tasks.title: Finalize Documentation and Packaging
tasks.description: Complete all project documentation, including setup and usage instructions, and finalize the `requirements.txt` file.
tasks.details: Create a comprehensive `README.md` file that explains the project's purpose, how to install dependencies from `requirements.txt`, and the exact command to run the script. Perform a final end-to-end test of the entire workflow.
tasks.testStrategy: Ask a colleague to clone the repository and follow the `README.md` instructions to set up and run the script. Confirm they can do so successfully without further assistance.

subtasks.title: Create README.md file
subtasks.description: Create a `README.md` file with instructions on how to set up and run the project.

subtasks.description: Ensure the `requirements.txt` file is up-to-date with all necessary dependencies.
